title: Sky commits its ETH, STETH and WBTC vault oracles to a single provider, treating oracle diversification as a fallback rather than a default
content:
A.3.7.1.1.4 requires that the Native Vault Engine collateral types ETH, STETH and WBTC "will specifically use the Chronicle v3 oracle solution, until at least January 1st 2026," and must migrate to the new version of Chronicle v3 when feasible. It then narrows the alternatives sharply: "Other oracle solutions, including diversified oracles, will only be considered until January 1st, 2026, and **only if** there are unresolvable security concerns with the Chronicle v3 oracles."

This inverts the usual risk posture. Price feeds are the single input on which every liquidation and Liquidation Ratio check depends, and the standard mitigation for that dependency is redundancy across providers. The Atlas instead standardizes on one, and admits diversification only as a response to a demonstrated, unresolvable defect.

The implied reasoning is that multiple feeds multiply the attack surface and the integration and monitoring burden rather than dividing the risk, and that a single well-scrutinized feed under a known operator is easier to secure and reason about. The wording "unresolvable" also sets a high bar: an ordinary security concern is expected to be fixed within Chronicle, not routed around.

The cost is concentration. Until the stated date, a Chronicle v3 failure is a system-wide event for Sky's largest collateral types with no pre-provisioned alternative, and the escape clause requires a judgement call at exactly the moment judgement is hardest to make.
description: Chronicle v3 is mandated until at least 1 January 2026, and alternatives including diversified oracles are considered only if unresolvable security concerns arise with Chronicle.
